content.comment_body: Q1 and Q2: when the LEDs are on, the power is off (negative DC). When the LEDs are off, DC power is present.
Why did you create a new topic? You already asked the same question earlier. See the previous thread: [url]

English is not my first language. First, it was suggested I had connected it incorrectly and that the [product_name] might be damaged. Then, I was asked for a basic wiring diagram for the lamp connection. If you want more details, I can try to explain again. I started this new discussion to figure out what's actually wrong with the [product_name]. You noticed that, straight out of the box, the outputs on the [product_name] are active when the LEDs are off, and inactive when the LEDs are on. I checked this with a meter you didn't accept (an analog one), and used a single 20mA LED without a resistor. Using the web-based management tool, I can set the inputs on either module to turn the outputs of the [product_name] on or off.

There’s no need to start a new topic for this. The diagram should only illustrate the wiring principle. Of course, you need resistors with the LEDs. It should clarify that the +24VDC output at the transistor terminals, and the corresponding ground (M-terminal) at Q1 and Q2, is the reference for 24VDC (0V).
Worrying about the external LEDs or the separate discussion isn't helping. Let's move on from this.
Thread closed because the question was posted twice. The other post with the same topic about [product_name] is already published in the [product_name] forum. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user reports an issue with a [company_name] communication module’s outputs: they appear on when the indicator LEDs are off, and vice versa. There is confusion about how the hardware’s outputs and indicator LEDs are supposed to behave. Attempts to clarify with measurements and further explanation did not resolve the technical issue, and responses focused more on forum conduct and wiring basics. The user’s frustration grew as the topic remained unresolved and was ultimately closed without a clear technical solution.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the hardware output signals (such as Q1 and Q2) to have clear correspondence with the LED indicators, and is seeking technical support focused on resolving the mismatch between observed LED and output states.
